TESTS and READERS: the Douay-Rheims follows the Vulgate's text and numbering, and the plan states a layer's own numbering only for Brenton. SOURCES: 'the existing slim verse row' cannot hold Brenton. eng-Brenton's vpl.txt has 315 lettered verse ids, among the added books TOB 14 (4:7a to 4:7l), ESG 88, SIR 12, 4MA 3 and DNG 2. Answer: say how a lettered verse is keyed and cited (for example 'Tobit 4:7h'), test it on a fixture line copied from the file, and count lettered lines in the count check.

src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py:203-207: an empty upstream verse reads as found, so a miss is reported as a hit. eng-web's Sirach has 24 lines with no text (1:5, 1:7, 1:21, 3:19, 10:21 and 19 more). Answer: the plan says an empty upstream line is not written, or reads not_found with the reason that the source has no text there; it says whether the count check counts those 24 lines; and a test pins 'Sirach 1:5'.

BASE and LIVE: no gated ship path runs the build on the box. tools/deploy.sh only snapshots, transfers, restarts and runs its four gates (lines 52-162). Run 2026-11-01-green-suite already recorded that deploy.sh never runs seeds and that the lead may touch the box only through it. So the build would be by hand, with no snapshot or revert of what it writes, and deploy.sh's on-box gate grades the engine before the layers exist. Two traps follow. A request between the restart and the build can cache an absent layer, as the base's bible() caches Bible([]) for a missing file (scripture.py:296-299), and the layer then stays empty until a restart. And a pin on the zip fails on any eBible rebuild, since every zip member carries its build time (all five were rebuilt between 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-10). Answer: name the gated path for the build (pin, write, re-run the gate, revert on failure, restart) and its order against the deploy; say whether an absent layer is cached; pin the vpl.txt member; and say what the lead does when the pin no longer matches.

MEMORY is not checkable as written. Answer: say whether ask and the console reach the added books, and by which forms (for example full names and canon.py's aliases only, with no prefix inference), and add base tests that such prose routes as it does today.

LAYERS says every 66-book reading is unchanged, but the tests name three full names (Genesis 1:1, John 3:16, Psalm 23:1) that no design breaks. The risk is in the alias and prefix tiers of Bible._pick_book (src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py:117-149). Measured with Ecclesiasticus, Judith and Esther (Greek) in the 66's index: 'Ecc 3:1', 'Eccles 3:1', 'Jud 5:1', 'Est 1:1' and 'Esth 1:1' go from ok to ambiguous. Answer: add these to the unchanged tests, or better, a test that every form of each 66-book name (the curated table, book_abbr, every prefix of three letters or more) reads as it did at the base.

TESTS: the count criterion cannot fail as planned. eBible's vpl.txt uses its own codes, not USFM: PSX for Psalm 151, PRM for the Prayer of Manasseh, 4ES, ESG, DNG and EPJ, and SOL EZE JOE NAH MAR JOH PHI JAM 1JO 2JO 3JO for 66-book codes. READERS: the prose guard is placed where it cannot hold. ask.find_ref returns the strict form 'word n:n' without validation (src/concordance/ask.py:778-780, _REF at 814), so 'yes sir 2:15 works for me' and 'meet me at the bar 3:15' are classified scripture at the base already (find_ref gives ' sir 2:15' and ' bar 3:15'). Answer: apply the guard wherever ask reads a ref found in prose, including ask.py:2082 and 2088, and add 'yes sir 2:15 works for me' and 'meet me at the bar 3:15' to the prose tests, each answered as at the base.

SOURCES, named exactly: eBible.org eng-web (the World English Bible, dedicated to the public domain, carrying every Catholic and Orthodox book canon.py lists for those layers) as the default layer, and eBible.org engDRA (the Douay-Rheims, the 1899 printing of Challoner's 1749-52 revision, public domain by date) on request. The strict PD-only gate gains a table keyed by source, not language, with each reason. The build tool, tools/build_canon_layers.py, imports only the standard library, writes its output as bytes with '\n' line ends, and is deterministic; it pins the sha256 of each extracted verse-per-line text file, never the zip (whose members carry their build time), and a changed text, an unreachable source or any other failure exits non-zero, so no build directory is added. Its listing entry in tools/box_builds.txt carries the output's sha256 (computed with the unit's own hash function), a memory cap, and its inputs: the book-code table, the committed verse counts and the pinned text hashes, which the path stages for it; src/concordance/build_pins.json carries the same hash.

BOOKS AND NUMBERING: eBible's own book codes (such as PSX, PRM, ESG, DNG, 4ES, SOL, JOH) are mapped by a committed table; a code neither mapped nor listed as deliberately skipped refuses the build. The expected verse count of each added book in each layer is committed, taken from checker-99's measurement at line 3, and the build refuses any mismatch. Each layer keeps its own numbering and every response says whose numbering it is; lettered verses, where an edition has them, keep their labels and are never folded into a whole number. An empty verse reads as missing, never as found.

THE GREEK ADDITIONS are served as the editions hold them: Esther (Greek) and Daniel (Greek) as books of the layer; Susanna as Daniel (Greek) 13, Bel and the Dragon as 14, the Prayer of Azariah as 3:24-90 in the WEB layer's numbering, the Letter of Jeremiah as Baruch 6; a request for the Additions to Esther resolves to Esther (Greek) with a sentence that the additions are read within it. canon.py's entries say which of these each is. A single-chapter addition is read in its own verse numbers mapped onto its span, and each response gives both: Susanna 1 is Daniel (Greek) 13:1, Bel and the Dragon 1 is 14:1, the Prayer of Azariah 1 is Daniel (Greek) 3:24; the name alone returns the whole span. The Douay-Rheims layer holds only the added books that have codes of their own in engDRA; its Esther and Daniel additions sit inside 66-book codes and are skipped and named, so a Douay-Rheims request for Susanna reads as a miss that says where that edition prints it.

READERS: the added books have a lookup of their own, consulted only when the 66's lookup recognises no book name at all, never when it finds a 66 book but not the chapter or verse; no name, abbreviation or prefix of a 66 book ever matches an added book, so Daniel (Greek) and Esther (Greek) are reached only by those names with '(Greek)' or by the names of their additions (Susanna, Bel and the Dragon, the Prayer of Azariah, the Additions to Esther), and a reference ambiguous among the 66 today, such as Jud 1:1, stays exactly as it reads. Every alias the 66 resolve today resolves exactly as at the base; Psalm 151 is reached by an explicit exception, since Psalms has no chapter 151 among the 66. The prose guard sits where text is read as a possible reference: ask.find_ref, the ask path's own reading of a reference (ask.py:2078-2090 at the base), and the console. UNCHANGED: the gate's assay, the floor and the moat hold; the full suite passes against the baseline; no file under data/ is committed; /languages, /capabilities and every 66-book reading are as before. LATER, named: Brenton's English and Greek Septuagint with the Psalms numbering map (the Septuagint run), and the Ethiopian layer's books.

LIVE: after the deploy and its build, the site and the MCP face read WEB Tobit 4:15 and Douay-Rheims Tobit 4:16 with their numbering and standing, Psalm 151:1, Susanna 1, John 3:16 and Ecc 3:1 as before; the engines' restart counts are read before and after by the lead.
